recipe.title: Plum, Almond & Cinnamon Yoghurt Pots
recipe.description: Creamy Greek yoghurt topped with ripe cinnamon-dressed plums and crunchy almonds, with just enough honey to round out the fruit's acidity while keeping the snack fresh, portable and simple.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 300 g; retail pot size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Use a thick strained Greek yoghurt so the pots remain creamy rather than watery during transport.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Choose ripe but still firm fruit that will hold its shape when diced.
ingredients.notes: Whole fruit does not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 24 g; retail pack size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Unsalted roasted almonds are suitable if available; otherwise ordinary unsalted almonds work well without additional cooking.
The small amount of honey rounds out tart plums without making the snack excessively sweet.

equipment.notes: Used to portion the yoghurt and almonds.
Used to dress the diced plums.
Pots with a separate dry compartment are ideal for keeping the almonds crisp during transport.

mise_en_place.instruction: Halve the washed plums around the stones, twist the halves apart and discard the stones. Cut the plum flesh into approximately 12 mm pieces, retaining the edible skins.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The plums are evenly diced into bite-sized pieces without being crushed or releasing excessive juice.

mise_en_place.instruction: Weigh 24 g almonds and roughly chop them into coarse pieces approximately 4-6 mm across.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The almonds are coarse enough to provide distinct crunch rather than fine crumbs.

procedure.title: Dress the plums
procedure.instruction: Place the diced plums in the small bowl. Add 1 tsp runny honey and 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, then fold gently until the fruit is evenly coated without crushing the pieces.
procedure.endpoint: The plum pieces are lightly glossy and evenly cinnamon-coated, with their shape still intact and no large pool of liquid in the bowl.

corrective_actions.condition: The plums are extremely ripe and begin breaking down during mixing.
corrective_actions.action: Stop mixing as soon as the cinnamon and honey are distributed and spoon the fruit directly into the pots.

procedure.title: Build the yoghurt pots
procedure.instruction: Divide the 300 g Greek yoghurt evenly between the two snack pots, giving approximately 150 g per serving. Spoon half of the cinnamon plum mixture over each portion of yoghurt. Do not stir the fruit fully through the yoghurt; keeping the layers distinct preserves a fresher texture.
procedure.endpoint: Each pot contains an even portion of thick yoghurt topped with distinct pieces of cinnamon-dressed plum.

corrective_actions.condition: The dressed plums have released substantial juice.
corrective_actions.action: Use a slotted spoon or leave excess juice behind in the mixing bowl so the yoghurt does not become watery during transport.

procedure.title: Pack the almonds separately
procedure.instruction: Divide the chopped almonds evenly between the two dry compartments or separate small containers, giving approximately half to each serving. Seal the yoghurt pots and almond portions securely and refrigerate until required.
procedure.endpoint: Both yoghurt pots are sealed and the almonds remain completely separate from the moist fruit and yoghurt.

corrective_actions.condition: The snack pots do not have separate dry compartments.
corrective_actions.action: Carry the almonds in two small separate reusable containers and add them immediately before eating.

plating.instruction: At the time of eating, scatter the chopped almonds over the plum and yoghurt. Eat immediately after adding the almonds so their crunch contrasts with the creamy yoghurt and juicy fruit.

storage.storage_instructions: Refrigerate the assembled yoghurt and plum pots promptly and use within 24 hours for the best fruit texture. Keep the almonds completely separate until eating. For transport to work or on a car journey, keep the yoghurt pots chilled in an insulated bag with an ice pack and do not leave them at room temperature for prolonged periods.

restaurant_quality_features: Ripe plums are lightly dressed rather than heavily sweetened, preserving fresh fruit character.
Cinnamon provides warmth and aromatic depth with minimal added complexity.
Thick Greek yoghurt creates a cool, creamy contrast to the juicy fruit.
Almonds are kept dry until eating so they retain a distinct crunchy texture.
Layered assembly preserves visual and textural contrast during transport.
nutrition_notes: Morning snacks have no minimum protein requirement.
Greek yoghurt contributes substantial protein and calcium.
Plums provide fruit, fibre and micronutrients.
Almonds contribute unsaturated fats, vitamin E, minerals and additional satiety.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary slightly with plum size and the exact yoghurt product used.
critical_success_factors: Use ripe but still firm plums so the fruit remains in distinct pieces.
Avoid transferring excess plum juice into the yoghurt pots.
Keep the almonds separate until immediately before eating.
Maintain refrigeration during storage and transport.
